title: Superpowers
subtitle: // the AI workflow that actually works

sections.heading: What is Superpowers?
sections.body: A complete software development workflow for AI coding agents — built on composable skills that trigger automatically.

sections.heading: Explosive Growth
sections.body: In just months, Superpowers became the fastest-growing AI dev tool on GitHub.

sections.heading: AI Agents Have a Problem
sections.body: Even the best AI models struggle with real software development.
bulletPoints: Models hallucinate and skip critical details
They rush to write code without understanding requirements
No testing discipline — ship first and debug later
Context loss across long development sessions

quote.text: It was a matter of describing how I wanted the workflows to go — and Claude put the pieces together.
quote.author: Jesse Vincent

sections.heading: What Spec-Driven Tools Do
sections.body: Frameworks like OpenSpec, SpecKit, and BMAD turn ideas into structured specifications.
bulletPoints: Convert conversations into task lists
Provide structured documentation templates
Focus on planning and specification only
Agent still left to figure out execution alone

sections.heading: Beyond Specifications
sections.body: Superpowers doesn't just plan — it brainstorms, designs, implements, tests, reviews, and ships. The complete pipeline.

sections.heading: The 7-Phase Pipeline
sections.body: Every project flows through a mandatory structured workflow. No shortcuts allowed.

sections.heading: Socratic Design
sections.body: Before writing a single line of code, Superpowers asks what you're really trying to build.
bulletPoints: Asks clarifying questions about intent
Explores alternative approaches
Presents design in digestible chunks
Proposes two to three implementation strategies

sections.heading: Sub-Agent Development
sections.body: Fresh sub-agents tackle each task with a two-stage review — spec compliance first, then code quality.

sections.heading: Agent Orchestration
sections.body: Multiple agents work in parallel across isolated git worktrees. No merge conflicts.

sections.heading: Hours of Autonomy
sections.body: Claude can work autonomously for hours at a time without deviating from the plan. Not an assistant — a structured engineer.

sections.heading: Enforced TDD
sections.body: Superpowers doesn't suggest testing — it mandates red-green-refactor on every task.
bulletPoints: Write failing test first — always
Minimal code to make it pass
Refactor only after green
Deletes code written before tests

sections.heading: Real-World Results
sections.body: Developers are shipping production-quality software with Superpowers.
bulletPoints: Command-line Space Invaders in Rust at 20K FPS
Landing pages with plasma shaders and 3D motion
Glass morphism and interactive carousels — fully generated
Quality that chat-based AI interfaces cannot match

sections.heading: Under the Hood
sections.body: A tightly engineered system powering autonomous development.

quote.text: Jesse is one of the most creative users of coding agents that I know — way ahead of the curve.
quote.author: Simon Willison

sections.heading: The Creator
sections.body: Built by Jesse Vincent — former Perl project lead, creator of Request Tracker, and founder of Keyboardio. Now reimagining how AI writes software.

sections.heading: Works Everywhere
sections.body: Install in seconds on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or OpenCode. Your agent just has superpowers.

sections.heading: Rapid Evolution

sections.heading: The Future of AI Development
sections.body: AI agents don't need better models — they need better methodology. Superpowers proves it.
